KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_CENTRAL_DESC: The acoustics in this shaft create unique echoing effects. Sometimes it sounds as if the walls are whispering.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_DEPARTURE_DESC: Lance was once trapped within this tunnel for an entire month due to a massive cave-in.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_EAST_DESC: The East Elevator was the first to connect Speranza to Acerra Spaceport.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_TRENCH_EAST_DESC: Taking this path back to Speranza you have to go right through the dreaded Caverna Ignis, so don't linger.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_TRENCH_WEST_DESC: This part of the trench tunnels was partially cleared only a few months back. Watch your head!
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_NORTH_DESC: When the North Elevator shaft was cleared, the diggers discovered dozens of trapped, disoriented first-generation ARC drones.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_CONTROL_DESC: Some walls in this tunnel show intricate patterns formed by the slow cooling of volcanic rock.
KeysToEntries.DAM_TRALICCIO_DESC: On first inspection, this seemed just like any old hatch – rusted hinges, cool to the touch. Who would have thought it was someone's home?
KeysToEntries.DAM_NORTHCOMPLEX_DESC: Sections of these tunnels exhibit a curious phenomenon where magnetic anomalies cause compasses to misbehave.
KeysToEntries.DAM_PUMPHOUSE_DESC: If you suffer from claustrophobia and fear of drowning, consider using a different hatch.
KeysToEntries.DAM_SPILLWAY_DESC: The tunnels in this area are almost impossible to keep open. Tremors and underground streams pose a constant challenge.
KeysToEntries.DAM_SWAMPSIDE_DESC: You'd think this elevator would win the "worst smell" category by a landslide, but the competition is surprisingly strong.
KeysToEntries.DAM_REDLAKEBALCONY_DESC: At the bottom of this elevator shaft, a rare type of fungi thrives on the metal-rich mud.
KeysToEntries.DAM_LAINES_DESC: Nasty water from the swamp perpetually fills the tunnel below this hatch so make sure the pumps are running.
KeysToEntries.DAM_SWAMPLIFT_DESC: The decomposing organic material from the swamp seeps into these tunnels and create pockets of dangerous gases.
KeysToEntries.DAM_OLDBARON_DESC: This tunnel runs past an underground cistern filled to the brim with red, iron-rich sludge.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_WEST_DESC: The air down here is thick and eye-watering. It carries the heavy, unmistakable scent of stale kerosene and rust.
KeysToEntries.SPACEPORT_SOUTH_DESC: This is one of Speranza's best maintained elevators - but it is also one of the least deteriorated.
KeysToEntries.BURIEDCITY_TRAINSTATION_DESC: An old access hatch near the train station. Last stop.
KeysToEntries.BURIEDCITY_COLLAPSEDSTORE_DESC: An adapted sewer entrance near a collapsed supermarket. All wares are on deep discount.
KeysToEntries.BURIEDCITY_OVERPASS_DESC: The traffic jams are absolutely ridiculous this time of year.
KeysToEntries.BURIEDCITY_OLDTOWN_DESC: Pretty sure there was a nice cafe around here somewhere.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BURIEDCITY_WESTERN_S: The Municipio metro station is closest to the sea. Water erodes its train tunnels and they require constant maintenance.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BURIEDCITY_SOUTHERN_: This used to be the Salini metro station. Shifting sands and seismic activity has collapsed most of it.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BURIEDCITY_NORTHERN_: The Nuovo Distretto station is the best preserved of the old metro stations.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BURIEDCITY_EASTERN_S: Centro Storico used to be the old town metro station. It's not very charming, but to be fair, it probably never was.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_RED_LAKES_HATCH_DESC: The tunnels in this area are almost impossible to keep open. The red, contaminated water pose a constant challenge.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_MOUNTAINCOMPOUND_LOA: Tucked away deep inside the facility, the doors in this station creak and squeak from disuse.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_MOUNTAINCOMPOUND_LOB: Swanky and comfortable, the walkways around this station feel like a meticulously curated experience.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_MOUNTAINCOMPOUND_SEE: After all this time, this marvel of indoor climate control still whirrs away undisturbed.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BLUEGATE_VILLAGEHATC: Built on top of an old well, the engineers building this hatch now share an impressive collection of ancient coins.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BLUEGATE_WRECKAGEHAT: After one glance at the surroundings, the foreman building this hatch made sure to use reinforced steel and extra-sturdy latches.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BLUEGATE_OLIVEGROVEH: The aromas drifting from the nearby olive grove makes this a particularly pleasant descent.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_BLUEGATE_CONSTRUCTIO: A surprising amount of boreholes already ran deep into the earth here, making this hatch a breeze to construct.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_CLIFFSIDE_AIRSHAFT_D: The engineers who connected this airshaft found it adorned with colorful chalk paintings from a nearby kindergarten.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_FOREST_AIRSHAFT_DESC: This airshaft is often clogged with fallen leaves, making for an escape that is as slippery as it is autumnal.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_HANGAR_AIRSHAFT_DESC: When this airshaft was connected to the Tubes, Apollo's crew spent several days clearing out packing peanuts and bubble wrap.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_OVERLOOK_AIRSHAFT_DE: The panoramic view from atop the hill makes up for the faint smell of bat droppings and stale grease.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_MOUNTAINCOMPOUND_HAT: Rusted mechanical arms loom like giants above this hatch.
Given its proximity to the sandbox, tube engineers recommend that you brush the dirt and grass off your shoes before entering this hatch.
This lonely hatch sits hidden in the tunnels beneath the cultural archives.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_RIVENTIDES_HATCH1_DE: The hinges creak under the weight of salt corrosion and seagull abuse.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_RIVENTIDES_HATCH2_DE: A last-ditch escape for many a Raider set upon by the riverbed.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_RIVENTIDES_HATCH3_DE: Some who've used this hatch claim to hear the gunshots emanating from Buried City.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_RIVENTIDES_ELEVATOR1: Built in convenient proximity to the nearby cranes, some speculate it may have have tempted a crane operator or two.
KeysToEntries.ID_EXTRACTIONPOINTS_RIVENTIDES_ELEVATOR2: For transporting heavy-weight goods, and even heavier stacks of paperwork.
